title: Cookie Login Redirects Disabled for Known API Endpoints
description: Learn about the .NET 10 breaking change where cookie authentication no longer redirects unauthenticated requests to known API endpoints.

data.text: In previous versions of ASP.NET Core, when an unauthenticated user accessed a protected endpoint, the cookie authentication middleware issued a 302 redirect to the login page. This was the expected behavior for browser-based applications, but it created problems for APIs — API clients expect a 401 Unauthorized, not an HTML redirect.

.NET 10 introduces automatic detection of known API endpoints. When a cookie-authenticated endpoint is matched as a known API path, an unauthenticated request now returns a 401 Unauthorized response instead of a 302 redirect. This is a breaking change for any API that was relying on the redirect behavior for cookie-protected API endpoints.

data.title: Breaking Change: Expect 401 Instead of 302
data.text: If your API client code handles 302 redirects for authentication, you will need to update it to handle 401 responses and trigger the login flow explicitly.
How Known API Endpoints Are Detected

The framework considers an endpoint a 'known API' if it is mapped via MapGet, MapPost, MapPut, MapDelete, MapPatch, or similar routing methods, or if it is decorated with [ApiController] or [ApiExplorerSettings]. Traditional MVC controllers and Razor Pages are not affected and continue to redirect as before.

data.title: API endpoints now return 401 instead of 302
data.content: A Minimal API endpoint protected by cookie auth now returns 401 when unauthenticated

data.text: If you need the old redirect behavior for a specific endpoint, you can override the automatic detection by explicitly setting the return type to IResult and issuing the redirect yourself, or by configuring the cookie authentication events.

data.title: Override to return a redirect manually
data.content: Explicitly return a 302 redirect for a specific endpoint

data.title: Migration Steps
items: Identify API endpoints that relied on 302 redirects for authentication.
Update client code to handle 401 Unauthorized responses.
If necessary, implement explicit redirect logic in the endpoint handler.
Update integration tests that assert 302 status codes for API endpoints.

data.title: Summary
points: Cookie authentication now returns 401 for known API endpoints instead of 302.
MVC controllers and Razor Pages are not affected.
Update API clients to handle 401 and trigger login explicitly.
Use explicit redirect logic if you need the old behavior for a specific endpoint.
data.takeaway: This breaking change aligns ASP.NET Core with common API conventions, where 401 is the expected response for unauthenticated API calls.
